content.comment_body: Good morning everyone, I previously used [product_name] to configure the cursor keys for controlling device levels. Unfortunately, these keys did not function as expected on the [product_name] operator panel. What should I do to get the cursor keys working with the equipment? Thank you for your attention.
Hello [user_name], Have you checked this discussion? [url] Best regards,

Hello [user_name], I reviewed the suggested topic and attempted the approach, but it did not succeed. Perhaps I made an error, so I am trying again: I assigned the cursor key with the setting "Momentary pushbutton (make)". Is that all, or is further configuration needed? I have attached an image showing my setup.
You need to press both the ESC and the cursor key simultaneously. The momentary (pushbutton) or contact (switch) settings only function correctly in simulation mode of [product_name] software.

I tried that as well, but the cursor keys never operate perfectly—even with the ESC key pressed. I have tested this on several [product_name] versions, and none work reliably. The equipment is used on the shop floor, where operators can't waste time dealing with buttons that don't respond consistently, so I ultimately added external pushbuttons to the design. It's unfortunate. I hope [company_name] will address this in a future update.
You can utilize the four function keys on the operator panel. These do not require simultaneous use with the ESC key.
I have not worked with the display unit myself, but I have heard that on this model, the cursor keys do function.

From my experience, using built-in cursor buttons as operator controls tends to cause problems. The reason is that dust and debris can enter the device via the buttons, leading to malfunctions. It's advisable to use high-quality external pushbuttons for operator input; otherwise, your efforts could be overlooked and the machine considered unreliable, all because of a few problematic buttons.
